key_insight: Ultra-high-precision analysis reveals subsurface buckling beneath 0.25 ML oxygen on Rh(100) and explains how nanoscale domains conceal the true periodicity of the 0.50 ML phase.
engineering_relevance: Accurate oxygen–rhodium surface structures provide a stronger foundation for atomistic models of this catalytically important material.
method: Quantitative low-energy electron diffraction (LEED) structure analysis
Variable-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and density functional theory (DFT)
Short-range-order simulations of coherent scattering from nanoscale domains
evidence_signal: LEED analyses achieved single-digit-picometer structural precision with Pendry R factors near 0.07 for both coverages, while simulations reproduced the near-extinction of diffraction spots.
watch_item: The 0.50 ML ground-state structure fragments into nanoscale domains even below 100 K, complicating diffraction-based identification of its periodicity and symmetry.
paper_title: Oxygen on Rh(100) revisited with ultra-high precision
